text:
Monday starts gray and a little raw. Warm air is already arriving overhead, but the clouds are stuck underneath it, so don't count on much sun. A few breaks late in the day are possible, and the high only gets to about 44. Skies clear tonight and we dip to around 31, so expect frost on the windshield Tuesday morning.

Tuesday is where the week turns. Mostly sunny and a good bit milder, with a high near 51. High pressure settles in and stays put, which means a dry stretch with highs in the mid 50s Wednesday and upper 50s toward Friday. Some spots could flirt with 60. Mornings stay chilly, in the 20s and 30s, but afternoons will feel more like mid-October than mid-November.

The next hint of rain is Sunday, and it's a shaky one. A front could bring scattered showers, but the forecasters see a real chance it slides past us and leaves little. I'd lean mostly dry.

Wear the jacket this morning and save the walk for Tuesday afternoon.
